slides.title: A joint-based control scheme with Cartesian-path input

visualInspection.notes: Cartesian-path input X_d and two derivatives enter trajectory conversion, which outputs desired joint position and derivatives. Feedback in the shown joint-based loop remains joint position; gains output torque. The common summing icon compresses several signals of different units and is not a literal dimensionally valid unweighted sum. X=[x y z]^T is position-only here. Footer 5. slides.title: Joint-Based Control with Cartesian Input:

visualInspection.notes: Inverse kinematics gives desired joint position; desired velocity J^-1 times desired Cartesian velocity; acceleration uses product rule J^-1 times desired acceleration plus time derivative of J^-1 times desired velocity. The printed J(Θ) does not explicitly say Θ_d: a derivative-consistent reference conversion must evaluate along the selected desired branch. Ordinary inversion requires square nonsingular J; derivative is of the inverse, not inverse of derivative. Cost, noise amplification and delay are listed. Footer 6. slides.title: Transpose-Jacobian Cartesian Controller

visualInspection.notes: Transpose-Jacobian diagram: δX→gains→virtual Cartesian force F→J^T→τ→arm. F=KδX,τ=J^TF. J^T is a force mapping, not generally an inverse displacement mapping. Same frame and work-conjugate coordinates are required. Footer 11. Actual readable 1800×1013 page pixels and extracted text inspected. slides.title: Model-Based Cartesian Control Law

visualInspection.notes: Model-based command ℱ=M_xℱ′+V_x+G_x; ℱ′ servo component has acceleration units in a translation-only task. Joint actuators realize command through torque rather than directly applying an independent endpoint force. Exact matching and nonsingular inertia are required for cancellation. Footer 14. slides.title: Adaptive control

visualInspection.notes: Adaptive control motivation: uncertain/changing payload, friction, wear, inertia and center of mass cause model mismatch and lost exact cancellation. Diagram is joint-coordinate θ not Cartesian χ: desired acceleration plus K_v Ė+K_p E yields τ′, dynamic model outputs τ. Adaptation receives E,Ė,θ,θ̇ and changes model. Footer 19.
